history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2137 ('Birla Mandir (Lakshmi Narayan Temple)', Jaipur) is a confirmed duplicate of seq 2075 ('Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple)', id 'birla-mandir-laxmi-narayan-jaipur') - the same temple: 'Lakshmi Narayan' is the same deity pair as 'Laxmi Narayan' (transliteration variant). Deduplicate downstream. Built by the B.M. Birla Foundation and inaugurated in February 1988. According to tradition the Maharaja of Jaipur gifted the land at the foot of Moti Dungri hill for a token sum of one rupee. The entire temple is carved from white marble, with three domes said to symbolise the three principal religions of India; its carvings include scenes from Hindu mythology, Gita and Upanishad verses, and portraits of figures such as Christ, Buddha and Socrates. The central idols of Vishnu (Narayan) and Lakshmi are carved from a single piece of marble. A Birla family museum and gallery sit beneath the temple, surrounded by gardens. (Note: one source says construction began in 1977; another says the temple was 'built in 1988' - the inauguration date, February 1988, is consistent across sources.)

name: Birla Mandir (Lakshmi Narayan Temple)
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is the 'Pink City' - founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, its rose-hued walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the historic heart of Kachwaha Rajput culture, home to the City Palace, Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, about 10-12 km south of the temple (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur Junction railway station, about 3 km away (verify).
travel.road: Tilak Nagar, at the foot of Moti Dungri hill on JLN Marg; reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning or evening visits are most pleasant.
